title: On-chain bounds and timelocks are accepted as substitutes for high signing thresholds
content:
The same substitution appears four times in this chunk. A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.2.3.1 recommends "at least seven of nine (7/9) signers, or an equivalent supermajority" for contract upgrades, then concedes that "[l]ower thresholds may be acceptable for highly constrained operations where execution scope is limited by on-chain parameter bounds." A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.3.2.2 tells Capital Allocation Multisigs to "implement on-chain constraints wherever feasible, including ... smart contract limits or parameter bounds." A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.3.2.3 requires that "[p]rotocol parameters controlled by Multisigs must be bounded through smart contract enforcement where feasible" and that major changes "be subject to timelock contracts or equivalent delay mechanisms." The general threshold exception (A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.2.2) grants relief where "parameters are tightly bounded and set by governance."

The principle is that two different things can limit damage: how many people must agree, or how much the agreed action can do. Signature thresholds are expensive — they slow every legitimate operation and require coordinating humans across time zones — while on-chain bounds are free at execution time and cannot be socially engineered.

Timelocks add the third dimension: not who acts or how much, but whether anyone can observe and intervene before it lands. A bounded, delayed action from a small multisig can be safer than an unbounded immediate action from a large one.

The design lesson generalizes beyond multisigs — reduce the authority rather than multiplying the approvers. The residual dependency is the phrase "where feasible," which appears in every one of these provisions and leaves the substitution's availability to the administrator's judgment.
description: Where execution scope is limited by parameter bounds enforced in contracts, lower thresholds become acceptable — trading human consensus for machine-enforced limits on what a signature can do.
